summary: This note describes Saint Thomas, one of the Virgin Islands in the Caribbean Sea and a former Danish colony. Together with Saint John, Water Island and Saint Croix, it forms a county and constituent district of the United States Virgin Islands, an unincorporated territory of the United States. The note gives Charlotte Amalie as the territorial capital and port, along with the 2010 census population and land area of the district.
one_line: Saint Thomas is a Caribbean island and constituent district of the U.S. Virgin Islands, home to the territorial capital Charlotte Amalie.
key_facts: Saint Thomas is one of the Virgin Islands in the Caribbean Sea.
Saint Thomas (Danish: Sankt Thomas) is a former Danish colony.
Saint Thomas, Saint John, Water Island and Saint Croix together form a county and constituent district of the United States Virgin Islands.
The United States Virgin Islands (USVI) is an unincorporated territory of the United States.
Charlotte Amalie is the territorial capital and port located on Saint Thomas.
As of the 2010 census, the population of Saint Thomas was 51,634.
The 2010 population of Saint Thomas was about 48.5% of the US Virgin Islands total.
The district of Saint Thomas has a land area of 32 square miles (83 km).
